title: 4-round AES-128: Fourth-round collision equivalence

target.description: AES-128 on 128-bit blocks. Consecutive inner rounds each include MixColumns; the round keys are fixed and unknown. The source explicitly specifies left-going ShiftRows.

setting.key_relation: Four fixed, unknown 128-bit round keys. The structural argument does not use their master-key dependencies, and therefore also applies to keys derived from any of the standard AES key lengths.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: Fix the other twelve input bytes; vary y at Y_(0,3) and use c=(c0,c1,c2) at Y_(1,3),Y_(2,3),Y_(3,3) as a parameter.

property.statement: Equality of the third-round projected bytes is equivalent to equality of tau=0E*t0 XOR 0B*t1 XOR 0D*t2 XOR 09*t3 after the fourth inner round.
property.quantifier: For the same fixed fourth-round key, s=Sbox^-1(tau XOR delta) is bijective in tau. Thus equality holds pointwise for every tested y; equality on sixteen samples alone requires the separate false-alarm heuristic.
property.scope: Four inner rounds with MixColumns in the last round. Coefficients are hexadecimal GF(2^8) constants; delta is fixed by the round key.

parameters.name: Inverse column coefficients
parameters.meaning: The first row of inverse MixColumns for the projected byte.

parameters.name: Four-round parameter representation
parameters.meaning: The third-round representation plus the fixed fourth-round offset; a structural description, not time or memory.

validation.description: The source gives an exact equality-preserving relation. Local FIPS-controlled checks cover96 round/projection samples; these component checks do not reproduce the associated distinguisher or its advantage.
